description: Every release-time check of the CTAS and WorldsIndex publishers and of the 'Validate and deploy site' workflow, with its class. Read by scripts/release_checks.py; see RESILIENCE.md.

classes.always_block: The hard core: secrets or banned keys in the public export, unmanifested files, checksum self-consistency. Blocks on every failure, from the first run: never in watch mode.
classes.integrity: The published data, or the code that loads and verifies it, is wrong: manifest closure, certificate self-consistency, provenance and receipt closure, provider-label publishability, missing or duplicated records, catastrophic data loss, front-end scripts that do not parse. Blocks once out of watch mode.
classes.advisory: Everything that cannot make the published data wrong: browser layout, payload budgets, accessibility, page copy, tests that pin specific real objects by name, interop round trips of derived exports, feed and changelog formatting, tooling tests. Never blocks a release or a deploy: a WARN line, the run's results, and one check-warning issue per check.

rule: Classify a new check by what its failure proves. If a failure can only mean that bytes readers download are wrong, missing, unsafe or unverifiable, it is integrity (always_block only for the hard core). If the published data could be right while it fails (a layout, a size budget, a pinned object, a derived export's formatting), it is advisory. When unsure, integrity: watch mode covers its first day.

watch.rule: A check (and each schema file of the schema validators) is in watch mode until it was first seen at least 24 hours ago AND passed N consecutive real releases (CTAS 4, WorldsIndex 3, deploy 3). In watch mode a failure is a warning whatever the class, except always_block. Promotion is recorded in check-history.json and is permanent; a changed schema file (sha256 of it and the schemas it references) starts a new watch period. Checks marked baseline ran on real releases before the history existed: when no history is readable they count as promoted.

fallback.rule: When a blocking check fails with the current site code, the release step runs once more with the code of the commit that produced the currently published release, on the same data; checks with fallback=false (secrets, export safety, restore safety, builder-side checks site code cannot change) never fall back, and a blocking check unknown to that code blocks.

parsers.unittest: FAIL:/ERROR: lines of Python unittest output; parts are Class.test
parsers.ctas-schemas: FAIL lines of scripts/validate_ctas_schemas.py; parts are the schema named on each line
parsers.worldsindex-schemas: indented failure lines of scripts/validate_worldsindex_schemas.py; parts are '<schema or file>: message'
